view.workbookViews.pageLayout.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.pageLayout, crates/ui-egui/src/paper_view.rs): the printed pages on a desk with margins, headers, footers and rulers; cells, selection and editing work on the pages as in Normal view; a header or footer is edited by clicking it (the Header & Footer tab). A file saved in it keeps it.

view.workbookViews.customViews.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.customViews {save, show, delete}); kept on the workbook, not as a hidden defined name, and not written to the .xlsx file.

view.show.ruler.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.ruler, a ribbon check box): the rulers of Page Layout view, which also set the margins when their edges are dragged; disabled outside Page Layout view.

view.show.gridlines.note: U:grid/view: a ribbon check box, as Excel draws it (gridcraft ribbon/view.rs checkbox).

view.show.formulaBar.note: U:grid/view: a ribbon check box; an application option (prefs.formulaBar), not saved with the workbook.

view.show.headings.note: U:grid/view: a ribbon check box, as Excel draws it.

view.zoom.zoom100.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.zoom {percent: 100}); runs the shared zoom command.

view.zoom.zoomToSelection.note: U:grid/view: gridcraft sends the grid size; without it the command fits 1200 x 700 px as gridcraft does.

view.window.newWindow.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.newWindow, windows.rs): another window on the same workbook, named Name:1 and Name:2; an edit in either shows in both, with one undo history. A window is an operating-system window of the application (the window service), as Excel and Word do.

view.window.arrangeAll.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.arrangeAll and the Arrange Windows dialog: Tiled, Horizontal, Vertical, Cascade, Windows of active workbook); the main process moves the windows, as gridcraft's interface does.

view.window.hide.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.hideWindow): the window goes out of sight and the workbook stays open; the most recent visible window comes forward. Disabled while it is the only visible window.

view.window.unhide.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.unhideWindow): Excel's "Unhide workbook:" list of the hidden windows; disabled when none is hidden.

view.window.sideBySide.note: U:grid/view: not in gridcraft (not checked against upstream); Excel's View Side by Side: this window and another next to each other (with more than two open, Compare Side by Side asks which), turned off by the same button.

view.window.syncScrolling.note: U:grid/view: not in gridcraft (not checked against upstream); Excel's Synchronous Scrolling: while two windows are side by side, scrolling one scrolls the other.

view.window.resetPosition.note: U:grid/view: not in gridcraft (not checked against upstream); Excel's Reset Window Position: the two windows viewed side by side share the screen equally again.

view.window.switchWindows.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft (view.switchWindows lists the open windows, the active one checked): the list is numbered as Excel numbers it ("1 Book1:1") and choosing one brings that window forward.

view.window.split.note: U:grid/view: checked against gridcraft: Split toggles frozen panes at the active cell (shown as frozen panes in that version).

view.sheetView.select.note: U:grid/main: View > Sheet View, built locally (not checked against upstream): named views of the sheet that each keep its AutoFilter and hidden rows and columns; Excel needs a shared workbook on OneDrive or SharePoint. The views are kept in the workbook, not written to .xlsx.

view.sheetView.keep.note: U:grid/main: saves the sheet's AutoFilter and hidden rows and columns into the view being viewed (see Sheet View).

view.sheetView.exit.note: U:grid/main: leaves the view and shows the sheet as it is in Default; what was not kept is dropped (see Sheet View).

view.sheetView.new.note: U:grid/main: a new view (View1, View2...) from the sheet as it is now, shown at once (see Sheet View).

view.sheetView.options.note: U:grid/main: Rename, Duplicate and Delete the view being viewed (see Sheet View).

view.appearance.displayTheme.note: U:grid/view: the application's own appearance (view.theme) is set in the app's settings, not per workbook; hidden here.

view.appearance.animations.note: U:grid/view: the application's own animation setting (view.animations); hidden here.

view.interface.size.note: U:grid/view: interface size (view.interfaceScale) belongs to the application's settings; hidden here.

view.interface.language.note: U:grid/view: interface language (app.language.set) belongs to the application's settings; hidden here.

view.macros.macros.view-macros.note: U:grid/main: hidden. View Macros lists and runs the VBA macros and scripts stored in a workbook; the application never runs code that came inside a document (a file's VBA project is kept as it is, not executed).

view.macros.macros.record-macro.note: U:grid/main: hidden. Record Macro writes VBA that the application would then have to run; it never runs workbook code. The Automate tab's actions are the application's own way to repeat steps.

view.macros.macros.use-relative-referenc.note: U:grid/main: hidden with Record Macro: it only changes how a recorded macro refers to cells, and there is no macro recorder.

view.macros.macros.note: U:grid/view: macros are VBA or scripts stored in a workbook; the application never executes workbook code, so Macros is hidden.

dialog.customViews.note: U:grid/view: Add… opens Add View (dialog.addView) for the name, as Excel does, and saves the view under it.

dialog.compareSideBySide.note: U:grid/view: not in gridcraft (not checked against upstream); Excel's Compare Side by Side, asked with more than two windows open.
